cim: The Family Office in the age of Artificial Intelligence
cim_eredeti: The Family Office in the age of Artificial Intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
The digitalisation of the Family Office is now a reality. With artificial intelligence, a new stage is beginning. AI makes it possible to analyse, synthesise and compare considerable volumes of information. It can speed up reporting, wealth consolidation, due diligence and portfolio analysis.

For Family Offices, which often operate with small teams, these capabilities are significant. But they do not change the essentials: AI must remain a tool. A powerful tool, but one that is directed, controlled and validated by humans.

Its role is to search, process, organise and present data in order to give professionals richer, more readily accessible information. But that data only becomes useful once it has been checked, interpreted and placed in context by people with the necessary expertise. AI provides information. It does not decide.

This distinction is fundamental in a Family Office. Family wealth is never simply a sum of assets and data. It requires an understanding of a family's history, its objectives, its businesses, its constraints, the relationships between generations and the sensitivities of each member.

This demands a high level of qualification, years of experience, multidisciplinary expertise and the ability to understand how complex issues interact. Finance, investment, tax, law, governance, real estate, entrepreneurship, succession – the Family Office must be able to engage with top-level specialists while keeping an overall view of the family's interests.

This expertise cannot be improvised. It is built through rigorous training, developed through experience and confirmed by dealing with complex situations.

The arrival of AI does not lower this bar. It raises it. To obtain relevant information, one still needs to know what to ask the AI, how to steer it, how to check what it produces and how to judge whether that information deserves to be used.

This is where the line is drawn: AI searches, processes and proposes data. The expert checks. The expert interprets. The expert decides. Decision-making and responsibility remain human.

No technology can replace the trust built over time between a family and those who support it.

We are therefore heading less towards an automated Family Office than towards an augmented Family Office, in which AI improves access to information without replacing those who have the competence and responsibility to use it.

The more powerful AI becomes, the more decisive the training and experience of those who direct it. Artificial intelligence can augment expertise. It cannot replace it.
